chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd, from 'Ali ibn Isma'il ibn 'Isa, and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, and Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), like it.
And he added to it: 'It remained with Umm Salamah until she died, may Allah have mercy on her.'

key_terms.أُمِّ سَلَمَةَ: Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet (s.a.a.w.)
key_terms.رَحِمَهَا اللَّهُ: May Allah have mercy on her (a common honorific for deceased women)

ai.seo_question: What did Umm Salamah keep from the Prophet's house until her death?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the physical manifestation of divine foreknowledge, where Umm Salamah preserved the specific dust of Karbala as a tangible link to Imam Husayn’s (a.s.) martyrdom. In Shia tradition, this act underscores the concept of *Ilm al-Ghayb* (knowledge of the unseen) granted to the Ahl al-Bayt and serves as a spiritual anchor for pilgrims seeking proximity to the Imam through his relics.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. My father narrated to me from Sa’d (ibn ‘Abdillāh), from ‘Ali ibn Ismā’īl ibn ‘Isā, Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, and Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from ‘Uthmān ibn ‘Isā, from Samā’ah ibn Mihrān, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: Jabra`īl announced the news of the killing of Ḥusain (a.s.) to the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) in the house of Um Salamah. While Jabra`īl was with the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.), Ḥusain (a.s.) entered. Jabra`īl said to the Prophet (s.a.a.w.), “Verily your nation will kill him.” The Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) said, “Show me the dust on which his blood will be shed.” Therefore, Jabra`īl took a handful of that dust and it was a red-coloured dust.
Um Salamah kept that dust until she died.
